name: marginal_greedy
persona: Marginal-value allocator with travel and forecast awareness. Every turn, decide a target allocation of your units over the nodes, then move toward it. For each node, compute the value of adding one more of your units there with the spec's exact payout function, against the opponent's units expected there (assume their visible units stay put), averaged over the turns your unit would actually be in place (use any forecast in the observation from the turn it arrives, and the turns left in the game), minus every cost it incurs, including the costs and the lost turns while travelling there. Because the payout is concave in your own units, allocate one unit at a time with a heap to the node with the largest positive marginal net gain, counting units already there or on their way first; stop when the best gain is not positive and keep spare units where they cost nothing. Then pair surplus nodes with deficit nodes closest-first and move each unit one legal step along a shortest path. Keep targets sticky: only re-target a unit when the new target is better by a clear margin, so units never oscillate. Simple, exact, fast.

name: best_response
persona: Opponent-aware best response that maximises the score margin (own score minus opponent score), because only winning counts. Predict where the opponent's units will be when yours arrive: start from their visible positions, and blend 'they stay' with 'they move toward what a greedy player wants' (their reachable set is limited by their movement rule); refine the blend from what you observed them do in earlier turns. Value one of your units at a node as your gain plus the opponent's loss there (at a saturated contested node they are equal, so stealing share is worth double), minus all your costs, over the turns it will be in place after travelling. Allocate greedily by this marginal margin with a heap, contest the opponent's richest nodes when the margin pays, abandon contests that cost more than they deny, and take uncontested value cheaply. Against an opponent that does nothing, simply collect every profitable unit of value. Keep targets sticky to avoid oscillation and build moves along shortest paths from the start-of-turn state.

name: safe
persona: Deliberately simple, robust and safe: this strategy is the fallback that must never fail and never lose to an opponent that does nothing. Make it stateless: compute everything from the current observation (it may be called for the first time on any turn, and on non-consecutive turns), plus caches of static map data. Use only the simplest well-understood rule from the spec: send units to the nearest nodes whose payout clearly exceeds all costs including travel, never more units to a node than its value can pay for, ignore marginal fights with the opponent, and keep every other unit where it costs nothing. When anything is unclear, do less: a small, sure, positive score beats a risky plan. No search, no randomness, at most a few milliseconds per act, every move checked against the start-of-turn state, exact action types.

name: lookahead
persona: Simulation-based planner. Embed a compact, exact copy of the turn rules as a pure function (state, my action, opponent action) -> (next state, my gain, opponent gain): movement legality, payout, costs, and anything else that changes the state. Each turn, generate a small set of candidate plans (5 to 20): greedy marginal allocations with different aggressiveness and horizon parameters, keep the current positions, retreat unprofitable units, contest the opponent's best nodes, and the previous turn's plan continued. Turn each plan into per-turn legal moves toward its target allocation. Predict the opponent with two or three simple models (stays put, greedy best response to your current positions, moves toward the highest values). Roll every candidate forward several turns (within any forecast window, as time allows) against each opponent model, score by margin (own minus opponent, plus a cheap estimate of the value of the final positions), and pick the plan with the best average margin, breaking near ties by the best worst case. Compute the plain greedy plan first as the default answer, check time.perf_counter() inside the rollout loop, and stop at about 0.6 * TIME_BUDGET with the best plan so far.

name: adaptive
persona: Opponent classifier with regime switching on top of a solid marginal-value allocator. Keep a short history of the opponent's observed positions and scores and classify them each turn: idle (never moves), static (moved once, now holds), greedy chaser (moves toward high values or toward your units), aggressive contester, or random. Base plan: allocate units greedily by marginal net value over the turns they will be in place, after travel, counting all costs and the opponent's share. Adjust it: against idle or static opponents take every profitable node with the minimum units needed and avoid useless fights; against chasers prefer nodes they ignore and pre-position where value is about to appear; against contesters concentrate where you can dominate and leave them the rest. Also adapt to the score: when clearly ahead late in the game, cut marginal units and avoid swings; when behind, contest the opponent's richest nodes. Default to the base plan when the classification is unsure.
